Household impact examples: the household API's answers (net income before and after, by programme, by measure and the earnings sweep) for the seven example households, each with every answer fixed in src/utils/exampleAnswers.js (no form default or prefill; rent £975 a month) and all nine candidate Autumn Budget 2026 measures selected (candidates modelled before the Budget, not announced policy), for 2027-28 to 2031-32. Regenerated on 26 October on Modal from this branch's own code (scripts/precompute_household_presets.py's calculation, one container per entry) on policyengine 6.10.2 (policyengine-uk 2.132.6): all 35 answers identical to the 25 October file. No marginal_rate_parts: this branch's API does not compute them. Hypothetical households; no survey records, ids or weights. To regenerate after #135, #169 and the household API changes merge, and on Budget day; pending review.

Percentiles (1st to 99th) of equivalised household net income, person-weighted, before and after each measure and the combined run, by year (2026-2031), from generate --only income_distribution --backend modal on the bundle's Microcosm UK 2024-25 dataset (policyengine 6.10.2, policyengine-uk 2.132.6). Income is household net income as the household calculator counts it (household_net_income less public spending in kind on the NHS, schools and transport subsidies, plus the business rates and stamp duty the model attributes to households), divided by the HBAI modified OECD scale; it differs from HBAI income (the decile charts and the Pre-measures forecast's median) mainly by including fuel duty and VAT. Each side is ranked against its own distribution. Each point is the mean income of the people in a band one percentile wide, never one household's figure; a band with fewer than 100 survey households has no row (none was dropped). No ids, weights or counts. No area below the UK. On the nine candidate Autumn Budget 2026 measures and their combined run (candidates modelled before the Budget, not announced policy). Every row is new and awaits review; read by the Household impact tab's 'Where you sit in the UK income distribution' card. Reviewed and signed by Vahid Ahmadi on 26 October 2026, covering these bytes.

Share of people (%) moving up, down or not at all a percentile and a decile of equivalised household net income because of each measure and the combined run, by starting decile and overall, by year (2026-2031), from generate --only income_distribution --backend modal on the bundle's Microcosm UK 2024-25 dataset (policyengine 6.10.2, policyengine-uk 2.132.6). Income is household net income as the household calculator counts it (household_net_income less public spending in kind on the NHS, schools and transport subsidies, plus the business rates and stamp duty the model attributes to households), divided by the HBAI modified OECD scale; it differs from HBAI income (the decile charts and the Pre-measures forecast's median) mainly by including fuel duty and VAT. Each household is ranked among everyone before the measure and among everyone after it. A share of movers drawn from fewer than 10 distinct survey households is left blank, with the matching share staying put. No ids, weights or counts. No area below the UK.
